do-i-still-need-to-file-a-boi-report.htm.text:
← Back to the BOI Reporting Exemption Checker

Do I still need to file a BOI report in 2026?

Short answer: if your company was formed in the United States, no — FinCEN's August 11, 2026 final rule (effective August 14, 2026) permanently ended the Corporate Transparency Act's beneficial ownership information (BOI) reporting requirement for every U.S.-formed entity and every U.S. person, regardless of size or industry. The only exception is a foreign-formed entity registered to do business in a U.S. state or Tribal jurisdiction — that kind of company must still file. Use the checker above to apply this to your own facts.

Why did this keep changing -- 2024, 2025, and now 2026?

The Corporate Transparency Act's reporting rule took effect January 1, 2024, requiring most U.S. companies to file. In March 2025, FinCEN issued an interim final rule exempting U.S.-formed entities and U.S. persons on an interim basis -- the exemption existed, but as agency policy that a future rulemaking or court order could still unwind. FinCEN's August 11, 2026 final rule (effective August 14, 2026) converted that interim exemption into a permanent one through formal rulemaking, which is a materially different legal footing even though the practical result -- no filing owed -- looks the same to most owners.

That is why a client alert or search result written any time before August 2026 may still describe the exemption as provisional rather than permanent, even though it was describing the correct practical outcome at the time.

DateWhat happened
January 1, 2024CTA's BOI reporting requirement takes effect; most U.S. companies must file
March 2025FinCEN's interim final rule exempts U.S.-formed entities and U.S. persons, on an interim basis
August 11, 2026FinCEN's final rule makes that exemption permanent (effective August 14, 2026)

I already filed a BOI report in 2024. Do I need to do anything now?

No. If your company was formed in the United States, FinCEN's August 2026 final rule permanently exempted it, so there is nothing left to file, update, or withdraw. A report you filed in 2024 does not need to be corrected, deleted, or resubmitted -- the exemption ends the obligation going forward, it does not undo the earlier filing.

My company was formed outside the U.S. Am I exempt too?

Only if it has not registered to do business in any U.S. state or Tribal jurisdiction. A foreign-formed entity that has registered to do business here is a "foreign reporting company" and the August 2026 rule did not exempt it -- it still must file, though only for beneficial owners who are not U.S. persons. Use the checker above with your own facts rather than assuming from the general rule.

That distinction — formed outside the U.S. versus registered to do business here — is the one detail that changes the answer, so run the specifics through the checker above rather than assuming from the general rule alone.

Could this reverse again?

It is legally harder to reverse than the 2025 interim rule was, because a final rule issued through notice-and-comment rulemaking cannot be undone with a single agency memo the way an interim rule can -- reversing it would need another full rulemaking or a court ruling. That is not the same as impossible. This page reflects the rule as of 2026-08-14; recheck FinCEN.gov before relying on an old answer, especially if you are reading this well after that date.

See FinCEN.gov's own BOI page for the current rule text if you are reading this well after that date.

No warranty. This page is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified attorney. Statutes and agency rules are amended without notice — verify the current rule directly with FinCEN.gov before you rely on any date here.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice.

Use the BOI Reporting Exemption Checker to apply this to your own entity's facts, or see the NY LLC Transparency Act tracker for the separate, state-level New York filing.

BOI REPORTING EXEMPTION CHECKER · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER · NOTHING UPLOADED

Do you still owe a beneficial ownership report?

FinCEN's August 11, 2026 final rule permanently exempted every entity formed in the United States, and every U.S. person, from Corporate Transparency Act beneficial ownership reporting. The requirement did not disappear entirely, though — a foreign-formed entity registered to do business in the U.S. must still file. This tool applies the rule to your facts.

Nothing is uploaded. Your answers are read in this browser and never leave your device — see the privacy note in the footer.

1. Where the entity was formed and whether it is registered here

2. Registration date and ownership

Choose where the entity was formed, then click Check.

Result

What this does not cover

  • Not a filing service. This tool only tells you whether the requirement applies and, if so, the deadline and which owners to report — it does not prepare, validate, or submit a BOI report to FinCEN's filing system.
  • Does not verify your facts. Formation jurisdiction, registration status, registration date, and each owner's U.S.-person status are all self-reported here. A mistake in any of them changes the answer.
  • U.S.-person status can be its own hard question. The rule's definition covers U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, and certain other categories — this tool does not walk through that definition and assumes you already know each owner's status.
  • Point-in-time rule. This reflects FinCEN's final rule as of 2026-08-14. Litigation or a future rulemaking could change it again; recheck FinCEN.gov before relying on an old result.

Common questions

Do U.S. companies still have to file a beneficial ownership report in 2026?

No. FinCEN's August 11, 2026 final rule, effective August 14, 2026, permanently removed the BOI reporting requirement for every entity formed in the United States and every U.S. person, regardless of size or industry. This is a permanent rule change, not another temporary pause.

Which entities still have to file a BOI report?

Only "foreign reporting companies": entities formed under a foreign country's law that have registered to do business in a U.S. state or Tribal jurisdiction by filing with a secretary of state or similar office. A foreign entity that has not registered to do business in the U.S. has no filing obligation.

If my foreign entity still has to file, which owners do I report?

Only beneficial owners (and, for a company formed on or after January 1, 2024, company applicants) who are not U.S. persons. A foreign reporting company still files its own company-level information even if every owner happens to be a U.S. person, but reports zero individual owners in that case.

What is the filing deadline for a foreign reporting company?

An entity that became a foreign reporting company before March 26, 2025 had an initial report due April 25, 2025. One that registers on or after March 26, 2025 must file within 30 calendar days of the earlier of actual notice or public notice that its registration is effective.

Is this legal advice?

No. This tool applies FinCEN's own published August 2026 final rule to the facts you enter. It does not verify your entity's actual formation jurisdiction, registration status, or any owner's citizenship, and it does not prepare or submit a filing. Confirm against FinCEN.gov's own BOI guidance or a qualified attorney before relying on this for an actual filing decision.

No warranty. This tool is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified attorney. You are responsible for reviewing and verifying its output before relying on it, and for confirming your entity's actual filing obligation before acting or not acting. To the maximum extent permitted by law, the authors accept no liability for any loss or damage arising from its use.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice. We do not promise uptime, backups of anything you type, or that a URL will keep working. Do not use this as a system of record — nothing you enter is saved anywhere by this tool.

Everything runs in your browser. Your answers are never uploaded; there are no accounts, cookies, or analytics vendors. Anonymous feature events (exemption_checked, example_loaded) are counted only in local storage on your device. The counts can be deleted with the button below. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honoured.

Already filed a report in 2024 and not sure what changed since? Read do I still need to file a BOI report in 2026? for the timeline from the original 2024 requirement through the March 2025 interim exemption to this August 2026 permanent rule.

Wondering why not just read FinCEN's own guidance instead? See this checker vs. reading FinCEN's guidance yourself.

Checking a New York LLC's state-level transparency filing instead? The NY LLC Transparency Act tracker is the one for that — a different, state-level beneficial-ownership disclosure law, unrelated to this federal rule.

vs-reading-fincens-guidance-yourself.htm.text:
← Back to the BOI Reporting Exemption Checker

This checker vs. reading FinCEN's guidance yourself

This names no specific firm or product. It compares a free browser tool against the generic method most entities actually use right now: searching "do I still need to file BOI", landing on FinCEN's own BOI page or a law firm's summary of it, and working out for yourself whether the August 2026 final rule leaves your entity with anything to file.

QuestionReading FinCEN's guidance yourselfThis checker
Whether the August 2026 rule is permanent or another pause FinCEN's news release says "permanently ends" but a stale search result or an alert written before August 14, 2026 can still describe the March 2025 change as interim, since that is what it was until this rule superseded it States plainly that the exemption for U.S.-formed entities and U.S. persons is now permanent, and names the rule and effective date it applies
Whether your entity is even in scope The rule distinguishes "formed in the U.S." from "foreign-formed and registered to do business in the U.S." in prose; you apply that distinction to your own entity Two questions — where the entity was formed, and whether it registered to do business in the U.S. — walk you to the same distinction without you having to parse the regulatory text
Your own filing deadline Both the fixed 2025-04-25 deadline and the 30-day-from-notice deadline are described; you work out which track your registration date falls on and count the days yourself Computes the applicable deadline from the registration notice date you enter, and flags directly when that date has already passed
Which owners actually get reported Easy to over-read as "report everyone" or under-read as "report no one," since a foreign reporting company files company-level information regardless, but reports individual owners only if at least one is not a U.S. person Applies that exact branch to the ownership answer you give and states it as a finding, rather than leaving it as a sentence to reinterpret
Not confusing this with a state-level filing A search for "beneficial ownership report" also surfaces state-level statutes, such as New York's own LLC Transparency Act, which is a separate filing under separate authority Covers the federal Corporate Transparency Act only, and links to the New York state tracker separately rather than conflating the two
Authority behind the answer The primary source itself — FinCEN.gov, its own news release, and the Federal Register notice are about as authoritative as a citation gets A rule-application aid, not a determination. Applies the same primary sources to your facts, but does not verify your formation jurisdiction, registration status, or any owner's actual citizenship
Where your entity's details go while you work this out Depends on how you research — a note-taking app, a spreadsheet, or a document that may sync to a cloud account Read in page memory only. Nothing is uploaded, and there is no server component at all
Filing the report itself FinCEN's own site is where you would file if a report is owed Never contacts FinCEN and files nothing — you remain the filer, and a required report still has to go through FinCEN's own system

Neither approach verifies your entity's actual formation jurisdiction, registration status, or any owner's U.S.-person status, and neither files anything for you. Both are only as good as the facts you bring to them, and both should be checked against FinCEN.gov directly before you rely on a deadline.

Common questions

Why not just read FinCEN's guidance myself?

FinCEN.gov is the primary source and this tool does not replace it — every answer this checker gives traces back to FinCEN's own August 11, 2026 final rule and the Federal Register notice. The friction is that the rule text describes categories in general while you still have to work out which category your own entity falls into, compute your own deadline from your own registration date, and figure out which owners the reporting requirement actually covers. The specific risk is search-result age: a page written before the August 2026 final rule, or a cached summary of the earlier 2025 interim exemption, can describe a broader filing obligation than the current permanent rule does.

Does this checker replace a lawyer?

No, and it is not trying to. This tool applies a published federal rule to the facts you enter and produces a likely outcome, not a determination of your entity's actual filing status. It is not legal advice and does not replace a qualified attorney. If your entity's formation jurisdiction is unclear, its registration status is contested, or an owner's U.S.-person status is genuinely uncertain, that is a question for counsel, not a web page.

How is this different from reading a law firm's client alert about BOI?

A client alert is written and reviewed by a licensed attorney, which is its real strength — this tool does not replace that either. The same date-drift risk applies: an alert written before FinCEN's August 14, 2026 effective date can still describe the March 2025 interim exemption as though it were provisional, when the August 2026 final rule made it permanent. This checker states which rule and effective date it applies on every result.

No warranty. This page is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice, and it does not replace a qualified attorney. Federal rules are amended without notice — verify the current rule directly with FinCEN.gov before you rely on any date here.

Best-effort hosting, no SLA. These tools are free, experimental, and may be slow, broken, moved, or taken offline without notice.

Use the BOI Reporting Exemption Checker to check your own entity, or read do I still need to file a BOI report? for the timeline from the original 2024 requirement through the March 2025 interim exemption to this August 2026 permanent rule.
